races.name: Sun Racing Free Tickets With Sun Club Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Premier Fantasy
runners_data.note: Recent pointing winner with good form who should sit prominently and benefit from the likely strong gallop
runners_data.spotlight: Fair pointer with a 6-15 record (2m4f-3m, good to soft-good to firm: tongue-tied for five) for Bradley Gibbs; arrives on the back of a victory in a small-field mixed open when a short-priced favourite and looks the type to make an impact in this sphere; respected on hurdle/stable debut.

runners_data.name: Tiger Rouge
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced unknown quantity making hurdles debut after poor pointing form, hard to assess
runners_data.spotlight: Half-brother to two winners, Skatman (useful 2m-3m2f hurdle/chase) and Rockbrook (2m-2m3f hurdle/chase); tailed-off last of seven in a point bumper in March and has plenty to prove on rules debut.

runners_data.name: Tiger Tobin
runners_data.note: Point winner making stable debut with prominent style, but form has been disappointing lately
runners_data.comment: Pulled up in a hunter chase on last year's rules debut and in a point in February
runners_data.spotlight: Maiden point winner in February 2024, but remains without further success and has struggled this year; faces a different test on hurdle/stable debut and will need to raise his game considerably.

runners_data.name: Brenda Lady
runners_data.note: Hold-up type claiming 7lbs who was well beaten on recent hurdles debut at longer trip
runners_data.comment: Appealing pedigree but this is a belated racecourse debut
runners_data.spotlight: Related to several winners, including Dare To Endeavour (useful 2m4f-3m chase); 100-1 when soundly beaten on hurdle debut at Ffos Las (2m, good to soft) a fortnight ago; step up in trip should suit but likely one for longer term.

runners_data.name: Polemon
runners_data.note: Former flat winner with hold-up style who showed early promise but form stalled in spring
runners_data.comment: Makes stable debut after absence but one of the likelier winners judged on Irish form
runners_data.spotlight: Three-time Flat winner (1m1f-1m4f) who showed promise in maiden hurdles but his progress stalled in spring 2025, pulling up on handicap hurdle debut and finishing well beaten on his final start for Denis Hogan in May last year; brought down at the first on stable debut after an absence this April (20-1), but still sets the standard with a mark of 110.

runners_data.name: River Don
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with moderate ability but gets uncontested lead in small field
runners_data.comment: Off mark at seventh attempt in points last month; cheekpieces on for rules/hurdle debut.
runners_data.spotlight: Off the mark at the seventh attempt in points when landing a five-runner maiden in April, but failed to build on that when tailed off and beating only one rival home on last month's hurdle debut over C&D; cheekpieces worn then quickly dispensed with and he needs to leave that effort well behind.

runners_data.name: French Diablo
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning from 168-day break after hanging badly on hurdles debut
runners_data.spotlight: Sent off at 4-1 for his debut at Musselburgh (extended 1m7f, good to soft) in November and travelled with some promise before hanging badly left; failed to back that up when beaten 44l at Newbury the following month but remains open to improvement and this longer trip could suit; hood added.

runners_data.name: Yellow Card
runners_data.note: Recent runner-up showing improved form, hold-up style suits likely pace scenario
runners_data.comment: 300-1 for a recent novice here and a long way behind Fairye Forth
runners_data.spotlight: Dual Flat winner (AW and turf; 1m1f-1m4f) but form slumped after a promising start for this stable; however, he produced a much-improved effort when runner-up at Ffos Las (2m4f, good) last month on his fourth hurdle start and a repeat of that performance would give him leading claims.

runners_data.name: Keep Off The Sugar
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who has regressed badly since promising bumper debut, long absence
runners_data.comment: Completely tailed off in two bumpers for this yard (hooded last time)
runners_data.spotlight: Made an encouraging start on bumper debut last March, but has gone backwards since and was tailed off on all three subsequent starts; offered little on last month's hurdling debut here (2m1f) after a break, and this longer trip needs to spark a major turnaround.

races.paceDynamic: River Don will likely lead from flagfall with no other confirmed front-runners in the field, setting a sustainable gallop over this extended trip. Premier Fantasy and Tiger Tobin should sit prominently behind the leader, while the majority including Yellow Card, Polemon, Brenda Lady and Keep Off The Sugar will track from midfield or further back. The lack of early pace pressure means River Don can dictate terms throughout, creating an even tempo that builds gradually to the finish. This tactical setup strongly favours hold-up horses who can produce late kicks, as they'll get the patient ride and strong gallop needed to showcase their finishing speed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If River Don sets uncontested fractions and the pace builds steadily from the back of the field
scenarios.body: The moderate early gallop allows patient riders to time their challenges perfectly, with late-running types getting the strongly-run race they need. Yellow Card and Polemon benefit most from this scenario with their proven closing kicks.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If Premier Fantasy or Tiger Tobin can stalk River Don closely and kick clear approaching the final flight
scenarios.body: The winner gets first run on the tiring leader while avoiding the traffic problems that can befall back-markers in small fields. Premier Fantasy's recent pointing success makes him best equipped to capitalize from this position.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Surprise Leader Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If River Don's moderate ability is offset by perfect tactical positioning and rivals fail to close
scenarios.body: The 5-year-old gets such an easy lead that he can find enough in the tank to repel late challengers over this stamina-sapping trip. His recent pointing win provides just enough confidence to sustain the effort.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos and Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If River Don stops quickly and prominent horses also empty, creating a messy finish
scenarios.body: The race falls apart tactically with the early leaders unable to sustain their effort, allowing an unfancied back-marker to pick up the pieces. French Diablo or Keep Off The Sugar could benefit from the chaos despite their recent struggles.

watchPoints.text: River Don gets such an easy lead that moderate ability may be enough to survive late challenges
Yellow Card and Polemon tracking too close early given their hold-up styles need patient rides
Premier Fantasy and Tiger Tobin both making stable debuts which adds uncertainty to their chances
French Diablo returning from long layoff may need the run despite prominent tactical position
Tiger Rouge completely unexposed over hurdles so market moves could indicate stable confidence

races.name: Edmundson Electrical Torquay Novices' Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Franigane
runners_data.note: Uncontested leader after 33-day break, hunter chase form suggests retained ability but stamina question over this longer trip
runners_data.comment: Found only Barton Snow too good in this last year; not as convincing on sharper tracks.
runners_data.spotlight: Sole win came in a 2m hurdle in February 2021 but long absences have interrupted his career in recent years; however, his hunter chase form reads notably well for a return to handicaps off what looks a workable mark on debut for Paul Nicholls and he won't be inconvenienced by any easing in the ground.

runners_data.name: Dunkerque
runners_data.note: Prominent runner in peak form with hat-trick completed 10 days ago, proven on good ground and suits the controlled pace scenario
runners_data.comment: 2m4f wins on good on last 2 starts (hurdle/chase); still feasibly treated; contender
runners_data.spotlight: Completed a hat-trick when winning at Kelso (extended 2m5f) ten days ago, making it 2-2 over fences, with all victories coming on good ground (handles soft); had a hard enough race there and shoulders a penalty here, so the booking of 5lb claimer William Shanahan looks a positive and another bold showing can be expected if this run doesn't come too soon.

runners_data.name: Doc McCoy
runners_data.note: Prominent style with 5lb claimer, chase record poor but class suggests he can exploit tactical positioning behind uncontested leader
runners_data.comment: Useful hurdler but hasn't offered a lot over fences and a while since he tried them
runners_data.spotlight: Five-time hurdle winner but 0-6 over fences; hasn't had much go his way since scoring in October but he was still in contention when unseating three out over fences last time in a race won by Dunkerque; now 10lb better off with that rival and he should be competitive given a change in fortune; forecast rain is a concern though.

runners_data.name: Vengeance
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner carrying bottom weight but 0-12 hurdle record and 47-day absence make him hard to fancy despite handicapper's opinion
runners_data.spotlight: 0-12 over hurdles and, while there have been hints of encouragement off a sliding mark, he hasn't looked like capitalising and now faces a stiff task from out of the weights on chase debut.

races.paceDynamic: Franigane will take the race up from the start with no other confirmed front runners in the field. Dunkerque and Doc McCoy will track behind in prominent positions, while Vengeance drops in last from his hold-up style. With only four runners and Franigane unopposed for the lead, the pace will be steady and controlled throughout, creating no early pressure on the front runner. This measured gallop strongly favours prominent runners who can track the leader and kick when the pace inevitably quickens, as there will be no early burn-up to weaken the field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace Suits Prominent
scenarios.trigger: If Franigane sets an uncontested lead with steady sectionals
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace allows prominent runners to conserve energy and strike late. Dunkerque's hat-trick form and Doc McCoy's class can exploit the tactical advantage of tracking a steady tempo.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Dominates Small Field
scenarios.trigger: If Franigane's 33-day break doesn't impact his stamina and he maintains rhythm
scenarios.body: With no pressure from behind in a small field, the leader can dictate throughout and prove hard to pass. His hunter chase form suggests he retains ability despite the layoff.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Jumping Errors Change Dynamic
scenarios.trigger: If the small field leads to tactical riding and mistakes at key fences
scenarios.body: Poor jumping or falls disrupt the race flow, allowing a different profile to benefit. The compact field means any error has magnified impact on positioning.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Style Surprises
scenarios.trigger: If Vengeance's sliding handicap mark creates unexpected value from the rear
scenarios.body: The steady pace allows the outsider to stay in touch longer than usual. His 0-12 record over hurdles makes this unlikely but the small field keeps him closer.

watchPoints.text: Watch Franigane's jumping rhythm early - any early mistakes could hand tactical advantage to Dunkerque tracking behind
Monitor Doc McCoy's confidence over fences given his 0-6 chase record and recent unseating
Observe if Vengeance can stay closer than usual in the small field given the likely steady pace
Check if William Shanahan's 5lb claim on Dunkerque proves significant if the finish becomes tight
Watch for tactical riding given small field - jockeys may wait longer than usual to make moves

races.name: Par Inn Novices' Handicap Chase

runners_data.name: Isle Of Sark
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with inconsistent chase form but the weak pace scenario suits his patient style perfectly
runners_data.comment: Didn't build on previous good Sedgefield third latest; mixed record over stayers' trips.
runners_data.spotlight: Flat/hurdles winner; ran encouragingly on his return to chasing but has failed to back up that effort in two starts since, taking record in this sphere to 0-8; admittedly well treated on best form.

runners_data.name: Black Occ
runners_data.note: Another closer who showed creditable effort last time and benefits from the likely lack of early pressure
runners_data.comment: Pulled up in 2 of 3 chase starts but creditable second in March (2m5f); should do better
runners_data.spotlight: Maiden who has inconsistent chase form (P2P3) but looks one of the likelier players provided he backs up latest effort, namely creditable third at Warwick (3m); runs off the same mark.

runners_data.name: Kenzo Des Bruyeres
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who struggled when ridden differently last time but may tire over this extended trip
runners_data.spotlight: 0-4 under rules; had a plausible excuse (perhaps unsuited by being ridden much less prominently than usual) on chase debut last time; remains the type to do well in this sphere, being a dual point winner.

runners_data.name: It's A Breeze
runners_data.note: Hold-up type from major yard but completion issues over fences are a significant concern
runners_data.comment: Fell four out on chase debut at Fontwell but he was close up at the time; dangerous
runners_data.spotlight: Maiden who is one of the lesser lights at his major yard and has failed to complete in two starts since switched to fences; on a positive note, reproduction of best hurdles form would give him place claims.

runners_data.name: Daring Plan
runners_data.note: Prominent runner in good form but lacks a win over fences and faces a step up in trip
runners_data.spotlight: Placed twice over shorter this year, runner-up at Fontwell (2m5f) last time; one of the main players on recent form but is no certainty to go one better, being 0-23 overall and not a certain stayer back up in trip.

runners_data.name: Ferando
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent runner but poor overall record suggests limited ability despite suitable style
runners_data.comment: Non-runner
runners_data.spotlight: Maiden who is 0-4 over hurdles and fences apiece (2m-2m6f); far from solid on form and chance largely depends on the effects of new trip.

runners_data.name: Winning Paddy
runners_data.note: Front-running tendencies but fading pattern and poor recent form make him vulnerable in the finish
runners_data.comment: 1-11 in Irish points; faces a tough task on British/stable debut switching to hurdles.
runners_data.spotlight: Record of only 1-11 in points and is far from solid on rules form (three attempts); however, may show the benefit of switching to handicap level off a modest mark.

runners_data.name: Bee's Kiss
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner stepping up from points but poor rules form and 8lb penalty create major obstacles
runners_data.spotlight: Has poor claims on rules form and is 8lb out of weights but may improve for this switch to chasing, being a point winner.

races.paceDynamic: Kenzo Des Bruyeres will lead from the front as the only confirmed pace-setter, with prominent runners Daring Plan, Ferando and Winning Paddy tracking behind but unlikely to pressure the leader early in this 3m2f test. The sustainable gallop will allow hold-up horses Isle Of Sark, Black Occ, It's A Breeze and Bee's Kiss to stay in touch through the middle stages. Over this staying trip with limited pace pressure, the race clearly favours hold-up horses who can produce late surges, as the early leaders will have done plenty of work by the closing stages.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If Kenzo Des Bruyeres sets his usual steady gallop and the prominent runners don't apply early pressure
scenarios.body: The lack of pace allows closers to conserve energy and time their challenges perfectly in the straight. Hold-up specialists can exploit tired leaders who've been working from early.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Sustains
scenarios.trigger: If Kenzo Des Bruyeres finds an ideal rhythm and his stamina reserves prove superior to the field
scenarios.body: The leader maintains his advantage as tracking horses fail to mount serious challenges and closers leave their runs too late. His front-running style proves perfectly suited to the weak pace scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Daring Plan or Ferando improve past their recent efforts and challenge Kenzo Des Bruyeres entering the straight
scenarios.body: The early tracking position proves ideal as they can respond to the leader's move while having enough left to resist late challengers. Their patient stalking tactics pay dividends.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Completely
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop becomes extremely sedate and all runners are still in contention turning for home
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint finish where any horse can win regardless of running style. Form and class become secondary to who finds the best turn of foot.

watchPoints.text: Kenzo Des Bruyeres setting too strong an early gallop could compromise his stamina reserves over this extended distance
It's A Breeze completing the course given his recent falls and unseats when switched to chasing
Isle Of Sark getting into contention turning for home after his disappointing recent efforts over shorter trips
Black Occ reproducing his last effort rather than reverting to his inconsistent pattern
Daring Plan handling the step up from 2m5f to 3m2f on his first attempt at this extended distance

races.name: Charles Darrow Mares' Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Queens Venture
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who completed a course double last August but recent form suggests she's lost some of her edge for this yard
runners_data.comment: Ran well for long way at Hereford this month, after a break; could have a say
runners_data.spotlight: Completed a double (2m6f/2m5f, good/good to soft) when winning here for Dan Skelton last August; she's run some reasonable races since for this yard but was a well-beaten second of two finishers at Fontwell recently.

runners_data.name: Porter In The Park
runners_data.note: Natural front runner with proven stamina at this trip, benefits from uncontested lead but has disappointed in last two outings
runners_data.comment: Run of place finishes halted latest; races off her last winning mark back down in class.
runners_data.spotlight: Runner-up at Warwick (3m2f, good to soft) in March under regular rider Cameron Johnstone-Baker and she's firmly in the picture on that form but two lesser performances have followed and she needs something extra.

runners_data.name: Jena d'Oudairies
runners_data.note: Improved markedly since fitted with first-time blinkers, two recent wins on good ground make her a major threat from prominent position
runners_data.comment: Led close home in new blinkers last month; still on a good mark and unexposed as a stayer
runners_data.spotlight: Won in first-time blinkers (retained since) at Taunton (3m, good) in April and had 9l to spare when following up at Stratford (3m2f, good to firm); also effective on soft/good to soft; climbing the weights but leading claims nevertheless.

runners_data.name: Miss Goldfire
runners_data.note: Returned to form with latest win under today's rider, unseated last time but effective fresh and handles this trip well
runners_data.comment: Bounced back to form with C&D win this month and remains on workable mark after 5lb rise
runners_data.spotlight: Returned to form to win under Ciaran O'Shea at Fontwell (2m5f, good) last month; unseated before the race got serious there last time; stays 3m2f and is effective on good to soft ground; capable of having a big say.

runners_data.name: Just A Memory
runners_data.note: Lowest-rated runner switching back to hurdles from chasing, recent chase runner-up form suggests retained ability despite rating
runners_data.comment: Has won over fences but no positives to take from her last three races
runners_data.spotlight: Won over fences here (2m5f, good to soft) last September and she returned to form when runner-up in a chase at Ffos Las (3m, good to soft) a fortnight ago; 0-6 over hurdles but showed promise in this sphere earlier in her career; could have a part to play if her good form continues.

races.paceDynamic: Porter In The Park is the only confirmed front runner in this field and will set an uncontested lead from the start. With Queens Venture, Jena d'Oudairies, Miss Goldfire and Just A Memory all showing prominent tendencies, they'll track Porter In The Park but none are natural pace-pressers. The moderate early gallop will allow Porter In The Park to dictate terms through the first two miles before the field closes up approaching the business end. This tactical setup strongly favours the early leader Porter In The Park, who can control the tempo and has proven stamina reserves to kick clear when challenged.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Porter Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Porter In The Park gets an easy lead and isn't pressed early
scenarios.body: The 9-year-old can dictate a steady rhythm that suits her stamina strengths, then quicken off that controlled pace when the field comes to her in the straight. Her proven ability at this trip on similar going makes her hard to peg back when in front.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Strong Finisher Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes truly crawling and turns into a sprint finish
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace allows one of the classier horses to produce a devastating late burst that the front runner cannot match. Jena d'Oudairies or Miss Goldfire have the tactical speed to capitalize on a slowly-run race.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Porter In The Park weakens approaching the final flight after setting the pace
scenarios.body: Queens Venture or Miss Goldfire, tracking the leader throughout, can take advantage when the pace-setter's stamina gives out. Their prominent positions allow them to strike quickly when the opportunity arises.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Benefits Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If multiple runners make mistakes at crucial hurdles in the straight
scenarios.body: Just A Memory, racing off the lowest weight, can pick up the pieces if the principals falter over the final obstacles. Her recent chase form suggests she retains ability despite her low rating in this sphere.

watchPoints.text: Porter In The Park's jumping under pressure - any mistakes when challenged could end her chances quickly given recent disappointing efforts
Jena d'Oudairies' position turning in - if caught too far back she may struggle to utilize her finishing kick effectively
Miss Goldfire's settling early - needs to travel kindly for Ciaran O'Shea to produce her best finish
Queens Venture's response to pressure - her recent form suggests she may not find as much as before when asked for maximum effort
Just A Memory's hurdle jumping rhythm - returning from chasing could affect her fluency over the smaller obstacles

races.name: Clearance Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Centara
runners_data.note: Front-runner who should get an uncontested lead and can control the tempo with only five runners
runners_data.comment: Five chase wins last summer; second wind op; steps up in trip but needs to find more.
runners_data.spotlight: Highly progressive over fences in the first half of last season, winning here four times (2m, good to soft/good); 2m5f here appeared to stretch him last month following some time off; has a lower mark to work with back over hurdles and he could play a leading role back down in trip.

runners_data.name: Howth
runners_data.note: Prominent racer returning from 255-day break but excellent course record suggests readiness
runners_data.spotlight: Switched to hurdles for new yard last May-September and won four of his six starts (all on good ground), two of them over C&D (one a handicap); held in fourth of six at Plumpton last September when last seen but retains potential; yard among the winners and he could go well back from a break.

runners_data.name: American Land
runners_data.note: Proven at this course with prominent style that should get ideal position behind leader
runners_data.spotlight: Prolific between November 2024 and June 2025, with his four wins in that spell including two here; his progress seemed to stall subsequently but he ran well when second of five to a progressive winner at Chepstow (2m, good) last time and could be in the mix; effective on good to soft.

runners_data.name: Arctic Voyage
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who needs strong early pace to be competitive from the rear
runners_data.comment: Penalised for his clearcut Hereford win but has less to prove than most of these
runners_data.spotlight: Useful on testing ground on the Flat early in career and this 4yo has tapped back into that promise over hurdles this spring, winning a maiden at Hereford (2m, good) in April on his second stable start and following up in a C&D novice (good); trainer won this with Clearance, after whom this race is named, in 2022 and 2024; intriguing candidate back in a handicap.

runners_data.name: Morning Mayhem
runners_data.note: Another hold-up type who may struggle if the pace is too steady early on
runners_data.comment: 2m course winnner in March and looked shade unlucky over 2m2f at Stratford on latest start
runners_data.spotlight: Three wins for new stable last season (2m, heavy-good to soft) and he's continued in good form, beaten only 1l when fourth at Fakenham (2m4f, good) last month; the drop back in trip could help; firmly in calculations.

races.paceDynamic: Centara will lead from the start with no obvious competition for the early pace, creating a sustainable tempo that suits his front-running style. Howth and American Land will track in behind as the prominent pair, while Arctic Voyage and Morning Mayhem are likely to be held up at the rear given their hold-up styles. The lack of early pace pressure means this will develop into a tactical affair with a strong gallop from the final bend. This shape clearly favours the front-runners and prominent racers who can control the tempo and have first run on the held-up horses.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Centara Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Centara gets an easy lead and kicks for home at the right moment.
scenarios.body: His front-running style is perfectly suited to this tactical setup where he can dictate terms without early pressure. The hold-up horses will have too much ground to make up when the pace lifts.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Howth or American Land track the leader perfectly and time their challenge to perfection.
scenarios.body: Both have the tactical speed to sit close enough to Centara before delivering their finishing kick in the final furlong. Their prominent styles give them the ideal position to pounce when the pace quickens.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Success
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely strong enough to set up the race for a closer.
scenarios.body: Arctic Voyage or Morning Mayhem would need the front three to go too fast early to have any realistic chance. Their finishing kicks could be potent if the leaders come back to them late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Surprise Tactical Switch
scenarios.trigger: If one of the supposed hold-up horses rides more prominently than expected.
scenarios.body: This would completely change the complexion of the race and could catch the market leaders off guard. Only realistic if connections have decided on different tactics from their usual approach.

watchPoints.text: Centara getting too easy a lead early and being able to dictate a soft pace throughout
Howth's fitness after 255 days off despite his excellent course form when fresh
Arctic Voyage and Morning Mayhem being too far back if the pace is genuinely steady
American Land's jumping which could be crucial if tracking the leader closely
Any tactical switches from the hold-up horses to race more prominently than usual

races.name: WestCountry Food Supplies Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Ugo Bingo
runners_data.note: Natural frontrunner returning from 52 days off with cheekpieces reapplied, but has proven difficult to win with recently despite dropping to last winning mark
runners_data.comment: A wilting fourth in this new headgear here last time and remains below his best
runners_data.spotlight: Has slipped to his last winning mark but he's proving difficult to win with and was well held at Wincanton in April last time; cheekpieces return and, while he copes with most ground, he's likely to be playing for minor honours at best.

runners_data.name: Zambezi Fix
runners_data.note: Confirmed hold-up performer but 11-year-old struggling badly for form since October with apprentice jockey taking 5lb off
runners_data.spotlight: Has been struggling for form since reappearing in October and offered little encouragement on April's return from just over two months off; has come a long way down in the weights and drops into a Class 5, but that's for good reason and he needs to turn things around.

runners_data.name: Peace Motivator
runners_data.note: Extreme concern as stable debutant who has failed to complete in all five hurdle starts including pulled up last month
runners_data.comment: Pulled up when 80-1 for recent stable/handicap debut; headgear switched here
runners_data.spotlight: Bumper winner for Olly Murphy in 2024 but has failed to complete in all five hurdle starts, including when pulled up on last month's handicap/stable debut; swaps hood for first-time cheekpieces but hard to recommend.

runners_data.name: Westerton
runners_data.note: Progressive hold-up horse fresh from close second at Warwick just 14 days ago, though 5lb rise for that effort asks more
runners_data.comment: Beaten 29l on stable debut at Uttoxeter 18 days ago.
runners_data.spotlight: Built on the promise of his seasonal return when a close second at Warwick (2m, good) last month, despite making a mistake at the last; a 5lb rise asks a little more, though Lewis Stones's 3lb claim helps offset that, and he still looks favourably treated on his best Flat form; with further progress likely, he's high on the shortlist.

runners_data.name: Ambassador
runners_data.note: Front-running type whose form has collapsed badly since August Cartmel win, returning from 50-day break under apprentice
runners_data.comment: Won at Cartmel in August but his form has nosedived since
runners_data.spotlight: Won at Cartmel (2m1f) in August but form has slumped badly since and he has shown no sign of a revival in two runs since returning from a break in April.

runners_data.name: Lord Cauvelliere
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist who showed improvement switching to handicaps at Ludlow 24 days ago after disappointing novice hurdle efforts
runners_data.comment: Handicap debutant who is interesting on the form of his bumper win last May
runners_data.spotlight: Good-ground bumper winner who failed to transfer that ability in three novice hurdle runs last year, but showed more switched to handicaps at Ludlow (2m, good) last month when keeping on after a mistake at the last; likely has more to offer and is one to consider eased slightly in the weights; unraced on ground worse than good.

runners_data.name: Get The Value
runners_data.note: Former course winner now 4lb below last winning mark but badly out of form since December, needs significant revival
runners_data.comment: Exposed 8yo who has been out of sorts in five runs following a break
runners_data.spotlight: Completed back-to-back wins last spring, including one here, but has been badly out of form since returning from a break in December; now 4lb below his last winning mark, but hard to make a case for in current form.

runners_data.name: Marhaba The Champ
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer returning from mammoth 207-day absence including Flat campaign, refused to start last time at York
runners_data.comment: Comfortably held since sold last July; 17lb below peak mark but no win since 2023
runners_data.spotlight: Largely disappointing for this stable under both codes and, after a brief respite on the Flat at Newbury in April, he refused to come out of the stalls at York last month, both times in this headgear; best hurdle effort when runner-up at Newcastle (2m1f, good) in October offers some hope on handicap switch, but current form is a clear concern.

runners_data.name: Jukebox Annie
runners_data.note: Struggling handicapper returning from 146-day break with little recent encouragement but gets significant weight relief
runners_data.spotlight: Has made little impact since switched to handicaps and, though well supported at Taunton (2m, good) in January, failed to justify the money, struggling a long way out and eventually pulling up; off since and now 14lb lower than her opening mark but can only be watched at present.

runners_data.name: Warfleet
runners_data.note: Bumper runner-up who has shown nothing since switching to hurdles, tailed off in both recent starts including 42 days ago
runners_data.spotlight: Showed promise when runner-up in one of three bumpers in 2024 but he's shown nothing worthwhile since switched to hurdles, finishing tailed off on both runs since returning from an absence in April; makes handicap debut off a lowly mark but with plenty to prove.

runners_data.name: Cogital
runners_data.note: Unpredictable 11-year-old fresh from AW efforts but showed promise when second over hurdles at Chepstow in March
runners_data.spotlight: Not the easiest to predict and well held on both starts on the AW since finishing a good second over hurdles at Chepstow (2m, good to soft) in March, ridden by Harry Atkins who can claim his 5lb allowance here; will not mind any rain and not out of this if in the mood, with one of his two hurdling wins coming over C&D.

runners_data.name: Hawa Jumeirah
runners_data.note: Dual flat winner making handicap hurdle debut with tongue-tie added after offering little in novice company
runners_data.spotlight: Dual Flat winner (1m2f/1m4f); has offered little in three runs over hurdles for this stable but may fare better now switched to handicaps with a tongue-tie added.

races.paceDynamic: Ugo Bingo will likely lead or set the early pace with Ambassador potentially tracking prominently, but with limited other natural pace horses this shapes as a steady tempo affair. The small field and lack of multiple speed horses means the pace will be sustainable rather than punishing through the early stages. The race will develop into a tactical battle from the back of the last hurdle where stamina and jumping accuracy become crucial. This moderate pace strongly favours hold-up horses who can produce a sustained finish, as the lack of early burn-up will leave plenty in reserve for the closing stages.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves as sedate as expected with Ugo Bingo setting modest fractions unchallenged.
scenarios.body: The patient tactics allow closers to arrive with maximum impact up the hill, while early leaders tire from the climb. Horses like Westerton, Lord Cauvelliere and Get The Value can time their runs perfectly.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent tactics prevail
scenarios.trigger: If Ugo Bingo and Ambassador inject more pace than expected, stretching the field early.
scenarios.body: The stronger gallop catches hold-up horses flat-footed and favours those positioned to strike from close range. Ugo Bingo's stamina and Ambassador's class could prove decisive if they handle the tempo.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Stamina test develops
scenarios.trigger: If the good ground plays slower than expected or the pace collapses completely in the middle stages.
scenarios.body: Newton Abbot's uphill finish becomes a pure stamina examination where previous course experience and staying power dominate. The race becomes a slog that suits horses with proven endurance.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos from mistakes
scenarios.trigger: If multiple horses make jumping errors at the later hurdles disrupting the rhythm completely.
scenarios.body: The race fragments into a survival contest where clean jumping and luck in running become paramount. This opens the door for outsiders who avoid trouble and benefit from others' misfortunes.

watchPoints.text: Peace Motivator must be watched closely for any market support given his record of five consecutive failures to complete over hurdles
Marhaba The Champ carries fitness concerns after 207 days off and refused to start last time, making his participation uncertain
Ugo Bingo's early tactics will set the tempo for the entire field given the lack of other confirmed pace horses
Westerton's jumping at the last hurdle needs monitoring after his mistake there cost him victory at Warwick last time
Ambassador's revival chances under apprentice Joshua Thompson need assessing given his dramatic form decline since August

runners_data.name: Matty's Mate
runners_data.spotlight: £135,000 3yo; brother to winners He Can't Dance (useful bumper/3m hurdle) and Musique De Fee (2m5f-3m3f hurdle); dam unraced half-sister to top-class 2m chaser Master Minded and two French Listed winners; represents highly notable connections; respected debutant.

runners_data.name: Mr Sunny
runners_data.spotlight: First foal; dam 1m/9.4f AW winner (RPR 58), out of maiden half-sister to 1m2f-1m4f Flat and useful 2m hurdle winner Middlethorpe; less interesting than stablemate Ocean Rose on breeding.

runners_data.name: Thepassingtyphoon
runners_data.spotlight: Dam runner-up in 2m/2m5f hurdles, out of bumper/1m6f Flat winner; yard has a poor strike-rate in bumpers.

runners_data.name: Winter Flight
runners_data.spotlight: Rules debutant who isn't particularly compelling on point form; the betting may offer further guidance.

runners_data.name: Ocean Rose
runners_data.spotlight: 10,000euros foal; dam bumper/2m4f hurdle winner, sister to winners Twelve Roses (useful bumper and 2m3f-2m5f hurdle/chase) and Cinderella Rose (bumper/2m-2m5f hurdle), out of bumper winner, is granddaughter of Stayers' Hurdle winner Rose Ravine; likely type on breeding.

runners_data.name: Megatothemax
runners_data.spotlight: Closely related to winners Rathhill (useful 2m hurdle) and Vegas Blue (bumper including Listed/2m3f hurdle), half-sister to bumper/hurdle winner Josie Abbing; dam maiden close relative of top-class jumper up to 3m1f Bellshill; stable 1-1 in bumpers this term; interesting newcomer.

runners_data.name: Roccana Rose
runners_data.spotlight: Dam placed in French 2m3f hurdles, half-sister to winners Honeysuckle (multiple 2m-2m4f Grade 1 hurdle including two Champion Hurdles) and Last Royal (bumper/2m5f hurdle); has had wind surgery; wears tongue-tie and hood on debut; heed the market signals.

runners_data.name: Three Of Spades
runners_data.spotlight: 5,000gns yearling; sibling to three Flat winners, notably Make Time (Group-placed 7f 2yo/1m; RPR 109); dam 7f winner (87), half-sister to 6f Group 2 winner Overdose; yard not associated with bumper scorers.

runners_data.name: Five Lanes
runners_data.comment: Ran out on last month's debut in British maiden point; may be best watched on bumper debut
runners_data.spotlight: The only contender with bumper form but sets a poor standard, having trailed home last of four at Hereford; ran out in a point prior to that rules debut.
